title: Ansel and the Thorn
premise: Quentin Blackwood, a royal food-taster who secretly sells forbidden charms to survive, finds his double life shattered when a mute child arrives at his door speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Thorn — an ancient magic the crown exterminated generations ago. As Quentin deciphers the child's warnings, he discovers the royal court itself is preparing to resurrect the war that once burned the world, and the only way to stop it is to reveal his own illegal magic and betray the king whose food he tastes. Torn between loyalty to the crown that shelters him and the truth that could save thousands, Quentin smuggles the child toward the last Thorn sanctuary while assassins close in. In the end, Quentin sacrifices his immunity-built body to complete a binding rite, dying as the war is unmade — only to wake, changed and mortal-magicless, in a kingdom where the child now speaks with a human voice and remembers him.
about_author: Mara Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals and poison ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery far older than themselves.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A routine morning tasting the king's breakfast establishes his careful life: numb tongue, hidden charms, five years of small sales in a city that hangs mages. He notes a strange bitterness in a spiced pear dish no one else detects. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. After court, he sells minor charms in the night market, showing his craft and his guilt. A buyer mentions rumors of 'green-eyed children' seen near the walls. He dismisses it. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A girl of eight appears at his lodgings, silent, eyes green as spring sap, and speaks three words in a language that makes his charms hum. She will not leave. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Charms Remember
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He tests the child, Wren, and realizes her speech predates kingdoms — the Old Tongue of the Thorn, extinct since the Purging. His grandmother's lullabies were fragments of it. Emotional beat: inheritance of a buried past.

chapters.title: Bitterness in the Pear
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Back at court, he identifies the same bitter note in the king's wine — a slow-acting Thorn-derived poison meant to look like illness. Someone inside the palace is dosing the king. Emotional beat: the taster becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: The Lord Chamberlain's Smile
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Lord Chamberlain Aldous Vane, who is administering the poison under orders of a faction wanting a pliable regent — and who has begun hunting the 'green-eyed child.' Emotional beat: cold ambition meeting superstition.

chapters.title: A Debt of Immunity
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Five years of tasting have built his resistance; the poison barely touches him, but Wren's presence at his flat is discovered by a palace informant. He must move her tonight or lose them both. Emotional beat: the double life collapses.

chapters.title: Running the Rooftops
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (rendered through sensation and image). Fleeing across the city at night, she perceives Quentin's small magic as warmth and the city itself as a wound. They reach the sewers beneath the old temple quarter. Emotional beat: trust forming without shared language.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Ash
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They seek Mother Ilsa, a disgraced court archivist living in the catacombs, who confirms the poison is a 'thorn-tithe' — a ritual component, not an assassination. The faction isn't killing the king; they're feeding something beneath the palace. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: Roots Under the Palace
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback chapters within her telling: the Purging, the surviving Thorn heart buried under the foundations, and the prophecy that a speaker would come to either waken or bind it. Wren is the last speaker. Emotional beat: history as burden.

chapters.title: The King's Table
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Summoned back to court, Quentin must taste for Vane while hiding what he knows. The king, half-lucid from the tithe, grips Quentin's wrist and whispers a warning in broken Old Tongue — the king knows more than anyone guessed. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking open.

chapters.title: A Charm Too Many
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Vane confronts Quentin privately, revealing he knows about the charm-selling and offers a bargain: deliver the child, keep his head. Quentin agrees aloud and lies with his eyes. Emotional beat: betrayal performed to prevent one.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Road
chapters.summary: Quentin and Wren's alternating POV. Flight north toward the last Thorn sanctuary with Vane's hunters behind them. Wren begins teaching Quentin the Old Tongue in stolen hours; their bond deepens into something like family. Emotional beat: tenderness on the run.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the river crossing, a hunter corners them; Quentin uses real magic openly for the first time, burning his cover forever. They escape but a palace rider witnesses it. Emotional beat: liberation and loss in one act.

chapters.title: Green Eyes in the Dark
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The faction accelerates the tithe; the thing beneath the palace stirs, causing tremors and blighted crops. Vane, unsettled, begins to doubt his masters even as he doubles the hunt. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Sanctuary of Thorns
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They reach the sanctuary — a living fortress of black bramble tended by three ancient wardens who test Wren and find her worthy. But binding the Thorn heart requires a blooded speaker and a willing vessel. Emotional beat: hope with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: Riders at the Bramble
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Vane's forces breach the outer thorns; the wardens fall one by one. Quentin learns the vessel must be someone saturated with old magic — and his five years of tasting tithe-poisoned food have made him the perfect vessel. Emotional beat: destiny as trap.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Taster
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Wren begs him not to do it; Quentin, who has never belonged anywhere, realizes this is the first place he chooses to stand. He accepts the rite as the sanctuary burns. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Binding
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren's POV. Speaking the full Old Tongue for the first time, she channels the rite through Quentin's body as Vane breaks into the inner grove. The Thorn heart wakes, recognizes Quentin, and is bound — the ancient war unmade before it can begin. Vane, seeing the thing he served, turns his blade on his own masters. Emotional beat: awe amid ruin.

chapters.title: Ash and Morning
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin dies in Wren's arms as the bramble blooms white. Grief, silence, the long walk back south with soldiers who saw miracles and don't know what to report. Emotional beat: hollow aftermath.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Spoke
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later: the poison exposed, Vane dead by his own hand, the kingdom uneasy but intact. Wren, adopted by Ilsa, tends a garden where a single white-flowered bramble grows. She speaks to it every day in the old language. Emotional beat: mourning as devotion.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Wren's POV. On midsummer's eve the bramble unfurls into a man — Quentin remade, magicless, mortal, remembering everything. Wren gives him the name Ansel, 'the one who stayed.' He tastes her cooking, and for the first time it is simply sweet. Emotional beat: belonging earned, at last.
